subject: incorporating patch existence in dynamic occupancy model

messages.author: 715ca9de5bff9dae
messages.subject: incorporating patch existence in dynamic occupancy model
parts:
Dear all,


I’m trying to run a dynamic site-occupancy model (cf section 13.5 in Kéry & Schaub 2012), while also incorporating information on whether any given site exists at each of my primary sampling periods. The reason I wish to do this is because throughout my dataset, new sites were introduced (created) each year, plus some have been destroyed over the course of the study.


The processes governing these site creation/removal events are very different biologically to those governing survival/colonisation within the site, and so I’d likely to distinguish between extinction caused by the removal of a patch vs loss of the species within a patch.

Currently, my way of incorporating that has been to create a binary matrix (existence) specifying for each j year, whether each i site existed, and incorporating this as follows:

 

    muZ[i,k] <- (z[i,k-1]*phi[k-1]*existence[i,k]) + ((1-z[i,k-1])*gamma[k-1]* existence[i,k])

    z[i,k] ~ dbern(muZ[i,k])

 

Thus z can never be non-zero in years where the site didn’t exist.

However, I’m concerned about the effect of this parameterisation on the behaviour of survival (phi) and colonisation (gamma). My goal is to have no information contributed from sites where the patch is destroyed to survival in that year (i.e, removing a site will inevitable mean it is no longer occupied, but I don’t want this to influence survival). I suspect that currently this is not the case, in which case it would seem that by using this model parameterisation I’m biasing the estimates of colonisation and extinction- the prior distributions for these parameters will provide more information than the data for sites that don’t exist.


Is this the case? And if so, is there a better way of calculating the parameters that I’m after?

 

Thanks for any advice


Sam

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: incorporating patch existence in dynamic occupancy model
parts:
Hi Sam,

The best thing you can do is use some of Marc's simulation code and modify it for your particular situation.  If you can recover the data-generating parameters, then you'll have confidence that your model structure works.

The way you've set up the model, your estimates of survival and colonization probability are population parameters for sites that exist.  If you were to calculate the finite sample proportions of survived sites using the latent states, unconditional on existence, they would be different since some of the sites were eliminated and for those sites survival was deterministically zero.

For example, let's say you had 100 sites and 80 of them were occupied in year 1.  In year 2, 20 of the occupied sites were eliminated and of the remaining 60 occupied sites, 40 of them survived to remain occupied.  The survival probability, phi, would be estimated as 40/60 = 0.67, while the finite-sample proportion calculated from the z latent states would be 40/80 = 0.50.  Obviously that last proportion includes both sites that existed and were eliminated, but the survival probably should not be biased.  Essentially, phi uses a denominator that accounts for site existence.
